text:
Priya (Support): Hey team, incoming from Acme — their integration is getting 404s on function/tool calls after we rolled the rename last night. They say it worked earlier today. Full error: `tool-not-found` on API call. Can we get eyes?

Carlos (AcmeCorp): Confirmed — we call `POST /v1/call_tool` with `{ "tool": "InvoiceGen", ... }` and get back: `400 / 404 depending on route` plus body: `{"error":"tool-not-found","detail":"no handle for InvoiceGen"}`. We didn't change anything on our side. :frowning:

Priya (Support): Thanks Carlos. What environment? Hosted or Dedicated? Client region? Also can you paste a full curl (redact keys)?

Carlos (AcmeCorp): Hosted (us-west). curl is:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_tool -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -d '{"tool":"InvoiceGen","args":{"invoice_id":"1234"}}'
```

Priya (Support): Got it. Jason/Marta — looks like we pushed a rename/alias sync last night that touched invoice tool handles. Could be alias propagation + casefold mismatch. Registry logs show a rename from `invoice-gen` -> `InvoiceGen` at 1719950000 and we may have TTLs on the client cache.

Jason (Eng Runtime): Thanks — I'm looking. Quick notes: our lookup flow does case-normalization but aliases in the registry have a separate canonical handle. If a rename happened, some prefix caches (edge-caches and dedicated-router caches) might still respond with the old mapping, and some clients do exact match vs casefolded match. Two likely repros: 1) client passes `InvoiceGen` (upper I/G) but our cache stored `invoice-gen` and the name->uuid mapping wasn't materialized in the local cache causing a `404` at the tool-resolver layer. 2) or alias backfill job failed halfway and left orphan alias records.

Marta (SRE): I see a spike of 404s from acme's org id at 1719993000-1719995000. Registry sync job showed a `partial-write` on worker-7 around 1719951200 but recovered. There are lingering TTLs on the edge cache (5m) but customer complains persisted longer -> suggests registry->client cache mismatch (client caches up to 24h).

Priya (Support): Carlos — can you try one thing for repro? Please call the lookup API directly and paste the response:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/lookup?name=InvoiceGen"
```

Carlos (AcmeCorp): Response:```json
{"error":"not_found","message":"no tool match for 'InvoiceGen'","suggestions":["invoice-gen","InvoiceGen_v2"]}
```

Jason (Eng Runtime): Interesting — the registry returns suggestions, so the name exists in registry but the exact handle isn't resolving to a live endpoint. Can you also call lookup with `invoice-gen`?

Carlos (AcmeCorp): ```json
// lookup?name=invoice-gen
{"ok":true,"tool":{"name":"invoice-gen","uuid":"t-0a1b2c3d","endpoints":["/v1/call_tool?handle=invoice-gen"]}}
```

Priya (Support): That confirms a case/canonical mismatch. Customer used `InvoiceGen` but the live handle is `invoice-gen`. We probably didn't set up the alias that maps the capitalized form to the canonical; or alias TTL didn't propagate.

Jason (Eng Runtime): Root cause hypotheses: rename was applied with canonical `invoice-gen` and alias `InvoiceGen` created but alias-backfill job skipped org-level ACLs for some tenants (race). Steps: 1) check registry write logs for alias creation (registry-bot shows `alias-create t-0a1b2c3d InvoiceGen` succeeded at 1719950020) 2) confirm alias propagated to edge caches — push a manual invalidation or bump cache version 3) run alias backfill for Acme org to ensure mapping is materialized.

Marta (SRE): I'll run a targeted cache purge for Acme's edge nodes and bump the lookup-service cache version for that org. Doing now.

registry-bot: scheduled: cache-purge org=acmecorp nodes=us-west-1,us-west-2 by=marta at=1719998203

Marta (SRE): Purge complete. Please re-test Carlos.

Carlos (AcmeCorp): Still 404 sadly. Lookup `InvoiceGen` still returns not_found.

Jason (Eng Runtime): Ok, purge didn't help — suggests alias wasn't in the registry alias-table for that org. Priya, can you run a quick DB query (read-only) on alias table for this tool/uuid in Acme org? If that's missing, we'll need a backfill + fix the writer. Query: `SELECT alias FROM tool_aliases WHERE uuid='t-0a1b2c3d' AND org='acmecorp'`

Priya (Support): Ran read-only: returns empty. The alias `InvoiceGen` isn't present at the org scope. But registry-bot showed it was created globally. Looks like we created the alias on global scope but not per-org (we recently changed scoping rules).

Jason (Eng Runtime): That explains it — client-side lookup uses org-scoped alias resolution first. Global alias alone doesn't bind for org-level requests. Fix: backfill per-org alias entries for any aliases created since the scoping change. I'll prepare a backfill job snapshot and run it for Acme.

Priya (Support): Action items: - Jason: run backfill for acmecorp and audit writer to ensure alias writes create org-scoped records (P0). - Marta: monitor for any other tenants with 404 spikes. - Priya: keep customer updated, ask them to switch to canonical handle `invoice-gen` as temporary workaround.

Jason (Eng Runtime): Starting backfill job for acmecorp now (job id bf-1719998300). Will post status.

registry-bot: job-start bf-1719998300 target=acmecorp aliases=invoice-gen/InvoiceGen created_by=jason

Jason (Eng Runtime): Backfill completed for acmecorp, wrote 1 alias mapping. Changed writer logic to also write org-scope. Rolling patch to registry-writer now (safe canary).

registry-bot: job-complete bf-1719998300 result=ok affected=1 duration=12s

Marta (SRE): I see the new alias in DB and it's in the lookup cache now. Carlos — can you retry?

Carlos (AcmeCorp): Works! Thanks, returning 200 and the tool runs. We'll update our integration to use canonical name while you fix writer. Appreciate the fast help. :clap:

Priya (Support): Great — marking as resolved for now. Jason, follow-up: PR to fix alias writer + add unit test for org-scope writes, and add an alert if aliases created globally without per-org entries for last 48h.

Jason (Eng Runtime): Will do. PR link when ready. Also adding a short postmortem note in #postmortems with timeline and the writer-change fix.

Priya (Support): Thanks all. Leaving thread open until PR merged.
